chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Talk shows and advice on surviving in the South Bronx
summary: On TV she sang 'There's Still a Little Starch Left in the Old Girl' and told people to get involved.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Yeah. Okay, you've also done a couple of TV talk shows haven't you?

Oh yeah, yeah. This all has to do, I guess, with "My Old Friends". There was alot of promotion from "My Old Friends" and I did alot of talk - I went on the air, radio and television, you know, to help promote the show. And being a senior too, a senior citizen there are allot of shows, "Over Easy" especially.
Yeah, twice. The first time I

did the show I sang "There's Still A Little Starch Left In The Old Girl Yet". I did the one song and we discussed the show and also a bit about my efforts in the community. And so I was invited back again just a few weeks ago in September to do "Over Easy" again. I flew out to San Francisco and the theme of that show was 'Volunteers'. Mainly about what I'm doing now community-wise. Right now the South Bronx seems to be in the news and they know about the South Bronx and so I guess they wanted to know how you survive in the South Bronx and how come I'm still here, you know. And I sang "They All Laughed" and "A Hundred Years From Today" on the show.
What did you tell them about how to survive in the South Bronx?

I said to get involved. I mean, everybody is not going to get up and leave. We've lost quite a few people. We lost alot of the population and anybody that comes to the Bronx, I mean, you know, they figure this is like Germany after the war. The devestation. You got abandoned buildings here and vacant lots, buildings that have been torn down. At one time here there was fire like every fifteen minutes. It was enough to frighten anybody.
